targets.authors: Brady WJ, Wills JA, Jost JT, Tucker JA, Van Bavel JJ
targets.title: Emotion shapes the diffusion of moralized content in social networks
targets.evidence_quote: We first conducted a pre-registered, large-scale direct replication of the moral contagion effect ( N = 849,266; see https://osf.io/gd734 ) ( 1 ).
targets.outcome_quote: In sum, the current research reveals that the findings of Brady et al. ( 1 ) replicate in multiple out-of-sample datasets using both dictionary-based and large-language model methods for measuring moral and emotional content, which highlights the general robustness of the moral contagion phenomenon.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The conclusion gives an overall replication verdict; this takes precedence over heterogeneity and the George Floyd exception.

targets.authors: Burton JW, Cruz N, Hahn U
targets.title: Reconsidering evidence of moral contagion in online social networks
targets.evidence_quote: We also tested Burton et al. ( 24 )'s key claim that moral contagion models perform no better than the nonsense “XYZ contagion” model.
targets.outcome_quote: Our findings also directly challenge previous claims made by Burton et al. ( 24 ) that moral contagion may not replicate well out of the original Brady et al. ( 1 ) sample, and that the moral contagion model performs “no better” than a nonsense “XYZ contagion” model.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly assess this published finding in new samples; verdict follows their stated overall comparison.

reasoning: New Twitter samples directly retest Brady et al. and explicitly retest Burton et al.’s model-comparison claim. Meta-analysis inclusions are not additional replication targets.
